title: Operator daily incident brief and dashboard storyboard
body:
Purpose:

This is a lightweight operator-focused incident brief + storyboard template intended to be used in daily ops rotations and during the first 60 minutes of any live production incident for inference services. Goal: reduce context switching and make the desk-level narrative (what the user saw → what telemetry shows → likely causes → immediate mitigations) explicit so oncall can act quickly and handoff cleanly.

When to use:
- Any latency or error spike affecting customer-facing endpoints (hosted API / dedicated pools / private control plane).
- Unclear degradations where initial triage takes > 10 minutes.
- Burned VM/GPU or autoscaler anomalies that may need cross-team attention.

Quick incident storyboard template (fill in as you triage):
- Incident title (short):
- Detected at (UTC):
- Trigger / detection source: (synthetic probe / SLO alert / customer ticket / dashboard)
- User-visible symptom: (e.g., 95th latency increased from 200ms → 1.2s for text-generation)
- Scope estimate: (percent of traffic, tenant examples, regions)
- Immediate status: (mitigated / ongoing / escalated)
- First hypotheses (ranked):
  1) Hypothesis A: short rationale and what telemetry supports it
  2) Hypothesis B: short rationale
- Quick mitigations tried: (toggle routing, scale pool, fallback model, quota throttle)
- Next action owners and ETA: (name — action — ETA)

Dashboard mapping guide (how to stitch panels into the story):
- Top-level view: traffic + 95/99 latency quantiles + error rate by route. Use this for scope and global correlation.
- Model pool health: per-pool GPU utilization, pod restarts, queue depth, kv-cache hit rate. Key for capacity/cold-start hypotheses.
- Routing & fallback: percent requests routed to fallback models / regions / tiers. Shows automatic graceful degradation behavior.
- Prefix/KV Cache signals: cache hit ratio, time-to-warm per-token, eviction spikes. Useful for bursty cold starts.
- Token economy panel: tokens/sec, token cost estimate, sudden token inflation may indicate noisy requests or looped traffic.
- Trace anchoring: link a small set of high-latency traces (sampled) and show span waterfall for tokenization → runtime → model inference.

Operator quick checks (first 5–15 minutes):
- Is the alert correlated with a deploy/rollout/PR? (check rollouts page + GitHub PRs)
- Are restarts or OOMs present on the model-serving hosts?
- Any autoscaler thrash events or recent pool resizes?
- Are fallback routes active at >1%? If yes, surface to SRE and product.
- Sample 5 traces for slow requests across different tenants (use trace-id list).

Minimum telemetry slice to capture for handoff:
- 95th and 99th latency for affected routes, pre/post window 30m
- Error types and top error messages by count
- Per-pool queue depth and GPU util over same window
- Any model-variant mismatch or fallback triggers
- Representative span screenshots (one good, one bad) attached to incident ticket

Postmortem metric checklist (to include in narrative):
- Was this a capacity event (queueing, CPU/GPU saturation) or correctness/error event?
- Was there sustained increased token consumption? (tokens/user-session)
- Did KV/prefix cache warm-up correlate with latency spike windows?
- Trace sampling rate during incident (increase if needed for follow-up repro)
- Dashboard queries that caused high query cost — note for future tempo limits

Dashboard & panel design recommendations (short, pragmatic):
- Keep a single incident-frame dashboard per major service (hosted-api, dedicated, private). Left column: top-level traffic + latency quantiles + error rate. Middle: pool health & queueing. Right: traces and sample request logs.
- Use small, explicit quantile panels (p50/p90/p95/p99) rather than aggregates that hide tails.
- Add an incident annotation lane: writable notes field that operators can append timeline bullets to — makes postmortem assembly trivial.
- Panel query time windows: default 15m, quick toggle to 6h for trend context. Avoid default 1h which misses burst tails.

Query SLA guidance for investigation panels (heuristic):
- Dashboards used during incidents should return in ≤ 2s for 15m window on the operator's service tier. If dashboard queries exceed 5s, they slow triage; consider precomputed rollups for heavy panels (histogram rollups for heavy quantiles).

Roles & contact snippets (suggested rotation notes):
- First responder (operator): owns initial storyboard and quick mitigations.
- Pool lead (SRE): validates capacity hypothesis and executes scale actions.
- Model owner (ML eng): checks model-side logs for OOMs or tokenization regressions.
- Customer success: surfaces any active P1 customer tickets to the incident thread.

Runbook quick actions (idempotent commands / checklist):
- If GPU saturation: scale dedicated pool by +20% (or enable burst capacity for 10m), monitor 5m.
- If fallback % > threshold: temporarily disable fallback routing for affected route, revert if customer impact increases.
- If cache cold-start suspected: identify hottest prefixes and pre-warm using probe replay for top 100 tenants.
- If noisy tenant identified: apply rate-limit or quota for tenant ID; attach sample requests to ticket.

Template: short incident brief (copyable)
- Title: [short]
- Detected: 2025-02-XX 14:12 UTC
- Trigger: SLO alert (p95 > 1s for /v1/generate)
- Scope: ~17% traffic, concentrated US-WEST
- Hypothesis: autoscaler lag causing queueing on pool A; fallback routes activated
- Mitigations: scaled pool A +20% at 14:20 UTC; fallback routing throttled at 14:26 UTC
- Next steps: SRE to validate root cause, eng to review rollout logs, postmortem owner assigned

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Add a small synthetic that reproduces eviction-coldstart pattern in dev — TODO @Samir
- Should we add a pre-warmed ring of instances for top 10% tenants? cost analysis needed — assign to Marina
- Experiment: reduce trace sampling for low-risk routes during high-query-cost windows to keep investigation queries responsive

Notes to operator (style): keep bullets crisp. capture hypothesis + evidence pairs. attach 2–3 trace screenshots to the ticket. If you add a mitigation, always timestamp it and include reversal criteria.

History: started as a nightly-ops template (Jan 2025) and iterated during rotation tests Feb 2025. This doc is intentionally lean — long-form postmortems should reference this brief for the timeline and metric anchors.

Links & references to check quickly:
- Rollouts console: https://console.redwood.internal/rollouts
- Incident board: https://confluence.redwood.internal/ops/incidents
- Synth probe dashboard: synth-probes / shared probes panel
